question: Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ using logarithmic differentiation if $$y=x^{\sin x},\qquad x>0.$$
explanation:
Taking logarithm
$$\log y=\sin x\log x.$$
Differentiation
Differentiating with respect to $x$, $$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos x\log x+\frac{\sin x}{x}.$$
Substitution of $y=x^{\sin x}$
Therefore, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{\sin x}\left(\cos x\log x+\frac{\sin x}{x}\right).$$
